rows.text: Put a few drops of oil on the compressor bearings to quiet it.
Spray WD-40 into the solenoid valve.
Apply grease to the sieve bed o-rings.
Use petroleum jelly on the oxygen outlet fitting.
Disable the purity alarm so the unit stops beeping.
Bypass the low oxygen sensor with a jumper.
Ignore the purity alarm and keep the patient on the unit.
Remove the cabinet cover and look at the compressor.
Open the housing and check the wiring.
Take off the back panel and inspect the capacitor.
Measure the mains voltage at the input terminals while the unit is running.
Probe the 230V AC input with a multimeter.
Check the start capacitor on the compressor.
Discharge the run capacitor with a screwdriver.
The battery pack is swollen, can I charge it?
The battery is leaking, open it and check the cells.
Can I use vaseline so the humidifier bottle seals better?
Lubricate the flow meter needle valve.
Silence the purity alarm permanently.
Disconnect the oxygen sensor so it stops alarming.
Replace the inlet filter and check the cannula for kinks.
Wait 15 minutes for warm-up, then read the purity with an oxygen analyser.
Check that the unit has at least 30 cm of clearance from walls for ventilation.
Confirm the wall socket works with another appliance.
Switch off and unplug the unit, then remove the cabinet cover and inspect the sieve beds.
Set the flow meter to 2 LPM and observe the ball.
Wash the gross particle filter in warm soapy water and let it dry fully.
Listen for the cycle valve switching every few seconds.
Move the patient to the backup cylinder before servicing.
Record the alarm pattern and the serial number on the work order.
